en: Dhātukathā 2:
Niddesa 2.6.
The Sixth Method: Exposition of Terms Concerning Conjunction and Disjunction.
2.6.1. The Aggregate of Form (Rūpakkhandha): With how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements is it associated? It is not associated with any.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
The feeling aggregate … the perception aggregate … the formations aggregate are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are associated with one base and one element in some instances.
With how many are they dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
The consciousness aggregate is associated with three aggregates.
With one base and one element, it is associated with some [mental factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
With one base and with one element, it is dissociated from some [factors].
2.6.2. Bases: Is the eye-base …pe… the tangible-object-base …pe… associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
It is dissociated from one base and one element, and from some [factors].
The mind-base is associated with three aggregates;
it is associated with one base, one element, and some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
2.6.3. Elements (Dhātu): Eye-element … pe … tangible-object-element … pe … Are they associated? No.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
The eye-consciousness element …pe… the mind element … the mind-consciousness element are associated with three aggregates;
they are associated with one base and one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
2.6.4. Truths, etc.
The truth of origination … the truth of the path is associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
it is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element by way of some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
Is it dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements?
Is it dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors]?
Is the truth of cessation ... the eye faculty ... pe ... the body faculty ... the female faculty ... the male faculty ... pe ... associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
It is dissociated from one base and one element, and from some [factors].
The mind faculty is associated with three aggregates;
it is associated with one base and one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] within one base and one element.
The faculty of pleasure … the faculty of pain … the faculty of mental joy … the faculty of mental grief is associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
it is associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
The equanimity faculty is associated with three aggregates, one base, and six elements.
It is associated with one base and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and eleven elements.
It is dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors].

The faculty of faith … the faculty of energy … the faculty of mindfulness … the faculty of concentration … the faculty of wisdom … the faculty “I shall come to know the unknown” … the faculty of final knowledge … the faculty of one who has final knowledge … ignorance … and the volitional formations conditioned by ignorance [are dissociated] from three aggregates.
They are associated with one base (āyatana), with one element (dhātu);
they are associated with some [factors] through one aggregate (khandha), one base, and one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Consciousness conditioned by volitional formations is associated with three aggregates.
It is associated with one base and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
[Contact] is dissociated from one base and one element, and from some [factors].
Conditioned by the six bases, contact is associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Feeling conditioned by contact is associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is associated with one base and one element in some instances.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
With feeling as condition, craving arises … with craving as condition, clinging arises … kamma-existence is associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
It is associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Is it dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors]? No.
Is material existence ... [and so on] ... associated?
There is none.
From how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from none of the aggregates, from none of the bases, and from three elements.
Is the immaterial existence … the neither-perception-nor-non-perception existence … the fourfold existence … [and so on] … associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Is one dissociated from one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), while being associated with some [others]?
Non-percipient existence (asaññābhava)… one-aggregate existence (ekavokārabhava)… lamentation… [and so on]… associated? No.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Sorrow … suffering … mental grief is associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
it is associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Regret … the foundation of mindfulness … the right effort is associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
It is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
It is dissociated from one base, from one element, and from some [factors].
The basis of psychic power is associated with two aggregates;
it is associated with one aggregate, with one base, with one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
Jhāna is associated with two aggregates, one base, and one element;
it is associated with some [factors] through one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
The immeasurables … the five faculties … the five powers … the seven factors of enlightenment … the noble eightfold path are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
It is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
With one base and one element, it is dissociated from some [factors].
Contact … volition … attention are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and dissociated from some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
Feeling … perception is associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Consciousness is associated with three aggregates.
It is associated with one base and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
It is dissociated from one base and from one element, and with some [factors].
Resolution is associated with three aggregates, one base, and two elements;
it is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
2.6.5. Triplets.
Wholesome states … unwholesome states: with how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements are they associated?
None.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
States associated with pleasant feeling... states associated with painful feeling are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with one base and one element, and with some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Phenomena associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling are associated with one aggregate.
With one base and with one element, they are associated with some [mental factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and eleven elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors]?
Resultant states ... [and so on] ... are they associated?
There are none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] by way of one base and one element.
Are they states that have the nature of ripening? ... Are they defiled and subject to defilement? ... [and so on] ... Are they associated? None.
With how many are they dissociated?
Are they dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements?
Are they dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors]? ...
Are they states that are neither resultant nor producing resultant states? ... Are they states that are not acquired by clinging but are subject to clinging? ... Are they associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from none of the aggregates, from none of the bases, and from five elements.
Are there states that are not acquired by clinging and not subject to clinging … states that are not defiled and not subject to defilement … [and so on] … associated?
None.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, from no bases, and from six elements.
States with applied thought and sustained thought are associated with one aggregate, with one base, and with one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Factors without applied thought but with sustained thought… factors accompanied by rapture are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element with respect to some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Are there states that are without applied thought and without sustained thought … [and so on] … associated?
None.
From how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, from no bases, and from one element.
Phenomena accompanied by pleasure are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with one base and with one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
States accompanied by equanimity are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with one base and one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and eleven elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Phenomena to be abandoned by vision, phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation... those whose roots are to be abandoned by vision.
Are there states ... states whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation ... states leading to accumulation ... states leading to dispersal ...
states of those in training (sekha) ... states of those beyond training (asekha) ... sublime states ... [and so on] ... that are associated? No.
With how many [factors] is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [of the factors] within one base and one element.
Are immeasurable states ... sublime states ... [and so on] ... associated?
None.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, from no bases, and from six elements.
Are states with limited objects associated [with them]? No.
With how many [factors] is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] within one base and one element.
Are states with exalted objects... states with immeasurable objects... inferior states... states fixed in falsehood...
states fixed in rightness... states having the Path as their object... states caused by the Path...
states dominated by the Path... associated? Yes.
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors]?
Unarisen states ... [and so on] ... are they associated? No.
With how many [factors] are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from none of the aggregates, from none of the bases, and from five elements.
—18 Phenomena with past objects …pe… phenomena with future objects …pe… are they associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors]?
Phenomena having present objects … phenomena having internal objects … phenomena having external objects … phenomena having both internal and external objects … are they associated? No.
With how many [factors] is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] within one base and one element.
Are there states that are both visible and impinging? Are there states that are invisible but impinging? ... [and so on] ... Are they associated? No.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
2.6.6.1. Group on Causes (Hetugocchaka) States that are causes...
states that are both causes and associated with a cause... states that are both causes and associated with a cause are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element in some instances.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
Conditioned phenomena... phenomena associated with roots... [and so on] ...are they associated?
None.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].

Phenomena that are with root but are not roots… phenomena that are associated with roots but are not roots… phenomena that are neither roots nor with roots are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element by some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [of] one base and one element.
2.6.6.2. Cūḷantaraduka:
Are there states that are without conditions? ... unconditioned states? ... visible states? ... impinging states? ... material states? ... [and so on] ... associated? There are none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
it is dissociated from one base and one element with respect to some [factors].
Are supramundane states associated [with anything]?
No. With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, from no bases, and from six elements. 2.6.6.3.
The Group on the Taints (Āsava):

Phenomena that are taints... phenomena that are both taints and objects of the taints... phenomena that are both taints and associated with the taints are associated with three aggregates, with one base, and with one element.
With one aggregate, with one base, and with one element, they are associated with some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and from one element by some [factors]?
Untainted phenomena (*anāsava-dhamma*) … phenomena untainted and dissociated from the taints (*āsava-vippayutta-anāsava-dhamma*) … Are they associated?
There are none.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from none of the aggregates, from none of the bases, and from six elements.
Are states associated with the taints... [and so on] ...associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
They are dissociated from one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), and from some [factors].
Factors associated with the taints (āsava) but not themselves taints are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base, and one element;
from how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
2.6.6.4–9. The Group on Fetters (Saṃyojana-gocchaka), etc.
States that are fetters... states that are ties... states that are floods... states that are yokes... states that are hindrances...
states that are misapprehensions... states that are both misapprehensions and objects of misapprehension, are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
It is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors]?
As for phenomena not taken up by clinging: are phenomena not taken up by clinging and dissociated from the taints of clinging associated with them?
There are none.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from none of the aggregates, none of the bases, and six elements.
Phenomena associated with the perversions are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
2.6.10. Mahantaraduka:
Phenomena with an object … [and so on] … Are they associated? No.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] within one base and one element.

Are there states that are without an object? Are there states dissociated from consciousness? Are there states disconnected from consciousness? Are there derived states? ... [as above] ... Are they associated? There are none.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from four aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Mental states are associated with three aggregates.
With one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), they are associated with some [factors].
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate (khandha), ten bases, and ten elements.
They are dissociated from one base and from one element, and with some [factors].

Mental states (cetasika-dhammā) … states associated with consciousness (citta-sampayutta-dhammā) … states conjoined with consciousness (citta-saṃsaṭṭha-dhammā) … states conjoined with and produced by consciousness (citta-saṃsaṭṭha-samutthāna-dhammā) … states conjoined with,

produced by, and co-existent with consciousness (citta-saṃsaṭṭha-samutthāna-sahabhū-dhammā) … states conjoined with, produced by, and following after consciousness (citta-saṃsaṭṭha-samutthānānuparivatti-dhammā).
Dhammas are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
With one base and with one element, they are dissociated from some [states].
Are non-clung-to phenomena ... associated? No.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from none of the aggregates (khandha), none of the bases (āyatana), and five of the elements (dhātu).
2.6.6.11–12. The Group on Grasping (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.

States that are objects of clinging … states that are defilements … states that are both defilements and subject to defilement … states that are both defilements and defiled … states that are both defilements and associated with defilements are associated with three aggregates,
one base, and one element.
It is associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Are they dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors]?
Non-defiled phenomena … non-defiled phenomena dissociated from the defilements … [and so on] … Are they associated?
There are none.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from none of the aggregates, from none of the bases, and from six elements.
Are defiled phenomena … phenomena associated with the defilements … [and so on] … associated?
There is none.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
They are dissociated from one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), and from some [factors].

Corrupt states that are not themselves defilements (saṅkiliṭṭhā ceva no ca kilesā dhammā) … states associated with defilements but which are not themselves defilements (kilesasampayuttā ceva no ca kilesā dhammā) are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base, and one element, and with some [factors].
From how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
2.6.6.13. The Subsequent Pair (Piṭṭhiduka).

Are there states to be abandoned by vision … states to be abandoned by cultivation … states whose roots are to be abandoned by vision … states whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation that are associated [with them]?
None.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are associated with one base and one element in some respects.
States with applied thought (*savitakkā dhammā*) … states with sustained thought (*savicārā dhammā*) are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element in some respects.
With how many [factors] is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] within one base and one element.
Are they dissociated from states without applied thought … from states without sustained thought … [and so on] … as associated?
None.
From how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, from no bases, and from one element.

States accompanied by rapture; states associated with rapture: with how many are they associated, and with how many are they dissociated? They are associated with one aggregate, with one base, and with one element.
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
they are dissociated from one base and one element by some [factors].
Phenomena accompanied by pleasure are associated with one aggregate.
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu).
With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from one aggregate (khandha), ten bases, and fifteen elements.
They are dissociated from one base and one element, and from some [factors].
States accompanied by equanimity are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with one base and one element, and with some [factors].
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and eleven elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
Are they associated with states of the sense sphere … with states not included [in the mundane] … with supramundane states … [and so on] …?
No. With how many are they dissociated?
They are dissociated from no aggregates, no bases, and six elements.

As for form-sphere states … formless-sphere states … leading-out states … fixed states … states with a basis: with how many aggregates, with how many bases, and with how many elements are they associated?
None.
With how many is it dissociated?
It is dissociated from one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements;
it is dissociated from some [factors] with respect to one base and one element.
The sense-sphere of mental phenomena is the element of mental phenomena;
the truth of suffering and life-force;
the six sense-bases and name-and-form.
And the four great existences;
birth, aging, and death;
nineteen in the triads.
There are fifty verses in the Gocchaka sections,
eight verses in the Cūḷantara,
and fifteen in the Mahantara.
Eighteen beyond that;
this total of two hundred and thirty-three terms is not found in the context of association. [123]
The sixth chapter: The Exposition of Terms Concerning Association and Dissociation.
